rules: Keep total script length strictly between 70 and 85 words so spoken delivery lands under 40 seconds.
The host hook line must be a single declarative sentence under 12 words that directly contradicts common intuition.
Place the mid-video prediction prompt between second 18 and second 22 of the timeline.
Limit titles to under 55 characters and include one emoji at the end.
Focus visual notes on macro engineering mechanisms or micro biological processes that can be drawn as cross-section diagrams.
Explainer sections must use real-world scale comparisons (e.g., 'weight of three cars') rather than abstract metric units.
formats_now: Hidden Everyday Mechanism: Explaining structural design choices in physical infrastructure or vehicle engineering.
Counter-Intuitive Animal Biomechanics: Dissecting extreme physical forces or physiological limits of megafauna.
Subtle Body Glitches: Revealing silent physiological processes happening inside the viewer right now.
hook_shapes: You think [X] happens because of [Y], but it is actually the exact opposite.
[X] is happening to your body right now, and your brain is completely hiding it.
[X] looks completely solid, but it is engineered to crumble when hit by [Y].
topic_areas: Dinosaur & Prehistoric Biomechanics (bite forces, locomotion limits, fossil preservation)

stop_doing: Writing multi-clause, complex opening hooks longer than 15 words.
Focusing on abstract astrophysics topics that rely on deep space imaging without tangible physical mechanics.
Using technical jargon like 'Kuiper Belt' or 'astronomers investigate evidence' in the first 5 seconds.
experiment: Test starting the script with a immediate direct second-person observation ('Your eyes are...') versus a third-person fact ('A T. rex bite...'), tracking if stayed_pct at 5 seconds increases by at least 5% for second-person hooks.
